notes: EMPTY-CASE, per instructions: every attempt returned duplicates:[] (info.count:0), so the item shape was never exercised — verdict is UNVERIFIED, not PASS. Tried three query shapes against the pool project (379335744 / PR-2005): free-text q.query='probe case' (200, empty), fully unfiltered q:{} (200, empty), and q.folder_ids='764093' scoped to the __readonly__ folder (200, empty). Did not trigger a dedupe run and did not invoke get_dedupe_status to disambiguate 'no duplicates' from 'feature flag off / scan never run' — that capability is out of scope for this probe of search_duplicates, but its existence is itself the documented way this ambiguity is meant to be resolved (its own guidance says exactly that, and list_duplicates's guidance repeats the same warning almost verbatim). One genuine error was hit: sending an empty JSON object as the body produced HTTP 400 {"error":"Invalid JSON data","details":"unexpected end of input at line 1 column 1"} — an envelope that matches NONE of the declared error shapes (the declared 400 is {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'} for a bad `p`; 401/403/500 use {success:false, error:{code,message,details}}; 422 uses {success:false, message:...}). This looks like a request-serialization artifact (an empty object apparently became an empty body) rather than a deliberate contract violation, but it is a real observed non-2xx shape outside the declared set, so it is recorded as error-envelope drift rather than diffed against the success schema. Sending {q:{}} instead avoided it. Name/path mismatch: the task states the live route is /ai-duplicates/search-v2 despite the capability being named search_duplicates. describeCapability's output for this capability carries no path/method field at all (that only appears for capabilities returned without a `name`), so the v1-name/v2-path mismatch could not be independently confirmed or explained through the MCP contract itself — nothing in intent or guidance mentions versioning or the backend route. Checked via searchCapability(entity=duplicate) for a sibling search_duplicates_v2: none exists. The full duplicate-entity family is entirely _v1: search_duplicates, list_duplicates, get_duplicate, get_dedupe_status, get_duplicate_source_test_case, resolve_duplicate, discard_duplicate. So the _v1 capability name is simply stale/uninformative relative to its v2 backend path, not evidence of a parallel v2 capability being missed. Separately: even had a match been returned, the declared 200 schema's `duplicates` items are unfalsifiable (bare {type:object}) — real field names live only in the `returns` prose list, so a full contract diff on item shape would not have been possible from the JSON schema alone regardless of data.
